validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION CONFIRMED, real and correctly classified. This is NGPL's (Kinder Morgan-operated) Gulf Coast Southbound Project Phase II, FERC Docket CP19-99-000: application filed Feb 28, 2019 (federalregister.gov 2019-09198), NOI to prepare an EA published Apr 15, 2019 naming the exact scope -- modifications at five existing compressor stations (Victoria, Wharton, Harrison, Angelina, Cass Counties, TX; no new pipe) -- (federalregister.gov 2019-07419), and confirmed completed/placed in service Mar 1, 2021 by both EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (Historical Projects tab, row 'NGPL Gulf Coast Southbound Project (Phase II)') and Kinder Morgan's own SEC 8-K (filed 2021-04-21, Q1 2021 earnings exhibit). NOT a duplicate: this is Phase II specifically, distinct from P2039 (Phase I, FERC CP16-488, completed 2018) and P2495 (134th Street Lateral, FERC CP20-14, a different NIPSCO-interconnect project entirely -- see cross_row_leads). Correctly classified as a gas transmission capacity-reversal/compression expansion, not a new build (hence LengthKnown=0 is right). Three concerns below (EndState, SegmentCost, Owner) all trace to the same likely root cause: whoever staged this row pulled facts from a Kinder Morgan earnings release that, in the same paragraph block, ALSO describes an unrelated adjacent KMI project (the ~$145M Acadiana Expansion serving Sabine Pass Train 6 in Cameron Parish, LOUISIANA) -- see the SegmentCost finding.

validity.recommendation: correct EndState/Province from Louisiana to Texas
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's EndState/Province='Louisiana' is wrong. This project's ENTIRE physical scope (five compressor-station modifications) is in Texas: FERC's Notice of Intent (federalregister.gov 2019-07419) names 'Victoria, Wharton, Harrison, Angelina, and Cass Counties, Texas' explicitly and unambiguously ('all locations are in the state of Texas'). Independently, EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook lists Beg_State=IL, End_State=TX for this exact project row. Independently, Kinder Morgan's own SEC 8-K (2021-04-21) states the project 'increases southbound capacity...to serve Cheniere's Corpus Christi Liquefaction facility in San Patricio County, Texas.' Three independent primary sources (FERC, EIA, KMI/SEC) all say Texas; none says Louisiana. The Agua Dulce Hub EndPrefecture/District value is fine to keep (it's a real South Texas gas trading point near Corpus Christi that both RBN Energy and the KM release associate with this project) -- only the state field is wrong. RBN Energy's own project database (the one harvested citation naming Phase II) oddly ALSO lists 'Agua Dulce Hub, LA' as the destination -- this appears to be an error in RBN's own dataset (or the origin of GEM's error, if RBN was GEM's original source), since Agua Dulce Hub is unambiguously in Nueces/San Patricio County, Texas, and three independent primary/regulatory sources agree it is Texas. Same likely root cause discussed in the SegmentCost finding: the sourcing researcher may have picked up 'Louisiana' from the immediately adjacent paragraph in KMI's earnings release describing the unrelated Acadiana Expansion project, which really is in Cameron Parish, Louisiana.

validity.recommendation: correct SegmentCost from $145,000,000 to ~$203,000,000 (KMI's own reported total project cost)
validity.researcher_notes: The recorded SegmentCost of $145,000,000 does not match any source for THIS project and is very likely a mis-transcription from a DIFFERENT, unrelated Kinder Morgan project mentioned in the same press releases. Kinder Morgan's own SEC 8-K (2021-04-21, Q1 2021 earnings exhibit) states, in the very next bullet after describing Gulf Coast Southbound: 'the approximately $145 million Acadiana expansion project...to serve Train 6 at Cheniere's Sabine Pass Liquefaction facility in Cameron Parish, Louisiana' -- a completely separate project. The SAME 8-K states, for Gulf Coast Southbound itself: 'NGPL's Gulf Coast Southbound project was placed in service on March 1, 2021. The approximately $203 million project (KMI's share: $101.5 million) increases southbound capacity...by approximately 300,000 Dth/d to serve Cheniere's Corpus Christi Liquefaction facility in San Patricio County, Texas.' The identical $203M figure (with the identical $101.5M KMI-share breakdown) also appears in Kinder Morgan's Q3 2020 earnings release (republished by boereport.com, 2020-10-21) describing the project as still under construction -- so this is KMI's consistent, repeated disclosure of the actual cost, not a one-off. Independently, EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook lists this project's cost as $176 million -- different from KMI's $203M (a ~13% gap, likely reflecting a different accounting basis/estimate timing -- e.g. FERC-certificate estimate vs. final actual cost -- not a rounding difference), but BOTH independent sources agree the true cost is far above the recorded $145M, and neither is anywhere near it. I'm proposing $203,000,000 as the corrected value (Kinder Morgan's own final, post-completion, as-built cost disclosure -- the more authoritative figure for a completed project), while flagging the $176M EIA estimate as a secondary data point in case an editor prefers the EIA figure or wants to research the source of the EIA/KMI gap further. Both the boereport.com republication and the SEC 8-K trace to Kinder Morgan as the ultimate origin (one operator origin, not two independent corroborators of $203M specifically) -- EIA is the one genuinely independent source, and it confirms the recorded $145M is wrong even though it doesn't land on the exact same number as KMI.

validity.recommendation: replace Owner1='Natural Gas Pipeline Co of America LLC (NGPL)' 100% with the actual current equity owners of NGPL
validity.researcher_notes: The recorded Owner1 lists NGPL as owning itself (100%), which is tautological -- NGPL is the pipeline entity, not its own owner. Per Kinder Morgan's SEC 8-K (2021-04-21): 'On March 8, 2021, KMI and Brookfield Infrastructure Partners L.P. (Brookfield) completed the sale of a combined 25% interest in Natural Gas Pipeline Company of America LLC (NGPL) to a fund controlled by ArcLight Capital Partners, LLC. KMI received net proceeds of $413 million for our proportionate share of the interests sold. KMI and Brookfield now each hold a 37.5% interest in NGPL. KMI will continue to operate the pipeline.' This dates from the same month Phase II went into service. Proposed: Owner1=Kinder Morgan, Inc. 37.50%; Owner2=Brookfield Infrastructure Partners L.P. 37.50%; Owner3=ArcLight Capital Partners, LLC 25.00%; Operator=Kinder Morgan, Inc. (per the 8-K's explicit operator statement). This is a SINGLE-SOURCE finding (KMI's own SEC 8-K) -- I searched for independent corroboration (a contemporaneous press release on businesswire.com, Kinder Morgan's newsroom, and general web search) but the KM investor-relations newsroom 403'd scripted access, a guessed businesswire URL for the Feb 2021 announcement didn't resolve, and this session's WebSearch budget was exhausted before a second source could be located -- flagging tier medium rather than high on that basis. The direction of the finding (NGPL is not self-owned; KMI/Brookfield/ArcLight are the equity holders) is not in doubt, only the precision of the exact percentages/date should be treated as single-sourced pending a second confirmation.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: My most recent independent dated evidence is Apr 2021 (KMI's SEC 8-K confirming the Mar 1, 2021 in-service date and describing NGPL as an ongoing, operated asset under a long-term take-or-pay contract commencing Apr 1, 2021), which is OLDER than the sheet's own LastUpdated (2023-07-27) -- I could not find anything dated NEWER than the sheet's last update despite trying: SEC EDGAR full-text search restricted to 2023-2026 for the exact phrase 'Gulf Coast Southbound' returned 0 hits (small, already-completed projects stop appearing in subsequent-year disclosures); FERC's Federal Register index has no further notices under CP19-99-000 after May 2019; and this session's WebSearch tool budget was exhausted, with DuckDuckGo (bot challenge) and Bing (no parseable results) both unproductive via direct curl. Absent any negative signal (no abandonment filing, no news of the compressor stations being taken out of service, and the project sits on a long-term take-or-pay contract structure that pipelines essentially never unwind), I'm confirming 'operating' on the strength of the 2021 in-service evidence and the lack of any contrary signal, but flagging explicitly that I could not independently verify post-2023 continued operation with a dated source -- an editor with FERC eLibrary or NGPL tariff/Form 2 access could close that gap.

cross_row_leads.facts: This exact URL is cited on P2541's gem.wiki page (footnote 9, 'fedreg'), but it is NOT about Phase II -- it is FERC's notice of NGPL's Nov 15, 2019 blanket-authorization request for the '134th Street Lateral Project' (FERC Docket CP20-14-000), i.e. P2495: 'an approximately 1.4 mile, 12-inch diameter pipeline lateral...in Cook County, Illinois and Lake County, Indiana' with a new NIPSCO delivery interconnect, estimated cost 'approximately $16.2 million'. Two things for P2495: (1) this is the likely primary source for its currently-uncited SegmentCost ($16.2M, matching the batch brief's MEASURED CONDITIONS note); (2) it states 12-INCH diameter, which conflicts with the sheet's recorded Diameter=20.00 in -- worth a dedicated spec check on P2495.

EIA's Historical Projects tab also carries 'NGPL Gulf Coast Southbound Phase I': Beg_State=IL, End_State=TX, Completed 2018-10-04, Cost $149M, Additional Capacity 460 MMcf/d, FERC Docket CP16-488. This independently corroborates the batch brief's existing flag that P2039's EndState='Louisiana' should be Texas (the EIA End_State field agrees with the route-geometry-based flag already noted for P2039, and is the same Texas-vs-Louisiana pattern found and corrected on P2541 in this shard).
